name: Dhauli Peace Pagoda
description: White pagoda built in 1972 on the site of the 261 BCE Kalinga War that transformed Emperor Ashoka toward Buddhism. Represents peace and non-violence philosophy.

name: Khandagiri and Udayagiri Caves
description: Jain rock-cut caves dating to 2nd century BCE, carved under King Kharavela. Originally 117 caves; 33 remain, including the famous Rani Gumpha (Queen Cave) with intricate double-storey architecture.

name: Lingaraj Temple
description: 11th-century shrine dedicated to Harihara (Shiva-Vishnu combined form) standing 180 feet high. Exemplifies Kalinga temple architecture with over 150 smaller shrines in the complex.

name: Nandankanan Zoological Park
description: 437-hectare zoo and botanical garden established in 1960, first Indian zoo in WAZA. Notable for white and melanistic tigers, home to conservation breeding center for Indian pangolins.

name: Rajarani Temple
description: 11th-century Kalinga architecture masterpiece 2.5 km from Lingaraj, renowned for intricate erotic sculptures rivaling Khajuraho. Unusually, not dedicated to any specific deity.

name: Grishneshwar Temple
description: An active Jyotirlinga shrine located adjacent to the Ellora complex, dedicated to Shiva. One of the 12 revered Jyotirlinga temples in India, built in traditional Hindu temple architecture.

name: Indra Sabha (Cave 32)
description: A Jain temple complex among the last structures built at Ellora, featuring multi-storey carved architecture with intricate carvings and detailed sculptural work representing Jain religious beliefs.

name: Kailasa Temple (Cave 16)
description: The largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world, carved from top-down from a single basalt cliff representing Mount Kailash. This 8th-century Hindu temple stands 32m tall and took over 100 years to complete, with an estimated 200,000 tonnes of rock removed.

name: Rameshvara Cave (Cave 21)
description: Possibly the oldest Hindu cave at Ellora from the late 500s, containing some of the most beautiful carvings on its pillars and walls dedicated to Shiva and Hindu deities.

name: Vishvakarma Cave (Cave 10)
description: A large Buddhist chaitya hall carved during the 6th century with intricate sculptural details. Features stone pillars and a stupa representing Buddhist architectural mastery.

name: Banasura Sagar Dam
description: India's largest earthen dam with sprawling clear-water reservoir surrounded by lush green hills and dotted with tiny islands. Located 20 km from Wayanad.

name: Chembra Peak
description: Wayanad's highest peak at 2,100 m. Viral heart-shaped lake at summit. Trek passes through waterfalls and lush vegetation with panoramic Western Ghats views.

name: Edakkal Caves
description: Two caves with 8,000-year-old Neolithic petroglyphs carved into stone. Located at 1,200 m elevation near Kalpetta. Name means 'a stone in between' referencing the dramatic rock formation.

name: Meenmutty Waterfall
description: Multi-tiered waterfall near Banasura Dam, 5 km away. Dense forest surrounds the cascades. Best during monsoon when water flow is strongest.

name: Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Part of Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Home to tigers, elephants, Malabar giant squirrels, and diverse bird species. Coffee, pepper, and cardamom plantations surround the sanctuary.

name: Brindavan Gardens
description: Man-made terrace garden on Kaveri River banks near Krishnarajasagara Dam, 12 km northwest of Mysore. Features botanical park, colourful musical fountains, and boating facilities.

name: Chamundi Hill
description: Hill temple 13 km from Mysore city at 1000 metres elevation dedicated to Goddess Chamundeshwari. Climb 1000 steps to reach the pristine temple with a 16-foot Nandi statue.

name: Mysore Palace
description: Built in 1912 for the 24th Wodeyar ruler, this Indo-Saracenic architectural masterpiece was the dwelling of the royal family. Famous for its evening lighting display.

name: Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens
description: Large zoo housing diverse animal species in spacious enclosures, located within the Mysore Palace grounds. Popular family destination with walking paths and animal displays.

name: Kanakakkunnu Palace Gardens
description: Historic palace with verdant gardens for serene walks. Hosts cultural programmes and performances, particularly during festival season.

name: Kuthiramalika Palace Museum
description: Built by Maharaja Swathi Thirunal, named for 122 wooden horse carvings on roof beams. Houses exquisite Kerala-style architecture, royal artifacts, and musical instruments.

name: Napier Museum
description: Historical museum in Thiruvananthapuram housing ancient sculptures, royal regalia, and artefacts. Neo-Gothic architecture set within the Thiruvananthapuram Zoo campus.

name: Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple
description: Over 3,000 years old, one of the world's richest temples. Principal deity is Lord Vishnu in eternal yogic sleep (Anantha Shayanam) on serpent Adisheshan. Seven-tiered gopuram dominates the skyline.

name: Haribaldev Jeu Temple
description: Ancient temple associated with the second Rath Yatra of Odisha. Built in 10th century, it holds significant place in local tribal and Hindu culture.

name: Mayurbhanj Chhau Dance
description: UNESCO-recognized Intangible Cultural Heritage martial dance form performed without masks. Baripada Chhau Mahotsav in April showcases this unique art form.

name: Simlipal National Park (Pithabata Gate)
description: Tiger reserve and biodiversity hotspot with dense deciduous forests, waterfalls, and wild animals. Entry via Pithabata Gate, 22km from Baripada. Open November to mid-June.

name: Deomali Peak Trek
description: Odisha's highest point at 1,672m on the Eastern Ghats. Moderately challenging trek through deep forests with panoramic views over valleys inhabited by Kandha and Paraja tribes. Summit camping available.

name: Summit Area Camping
description: Overnight camping on high-altitude forest clearing near the peak. Observe Eastern Ghats valleys at sunset, experience tribal cultures of surrounding villages, and spot indigenous forest fauna.

name: Tribal Museum Koraput
description: Repository of tribal culture from Kondh, Bonda and Paroja communities. Displays traditional textiles, musical instruments, stone sculptures, terracotta and embroidered shawls of Dongria Kondh artisans.

name: Kadmat Lagoon
description: Pristine shallow lagoon ideal for snorkeling, kayaking, and water sports. Glass-bottom boats, pedal boats, and sailing boats available for hire.

name: Kadmat Reef Walking
description: Walk across exposed coral reefs at low tide. Longest sandbank in Lakshadweep. Safe exploration of coral formations, clownfish, and parrotfish habitats.

name: The Wall — Dive Site
description: Dramatic underwater cliff face. Premier scuba diving spot offering wall-like coral reefs and encounters with pelagic fish and sea turtles. Only CMAS-certified dive school in India based here.

name: Gandhi Memorial Museum
description: Located in 17th-century palace. Preserves Mahatma Gandhi items and freedom struggle records.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
description: One of world's largest temple complexes. 4500 sq m, 14 gopurams, 33000 sculptures. Midnight ceremony: Sundareshwarar carried to Meenakshi's bedchamber.

name: Thirumalai Nayakkar Palace
description: Built 1636 by Tirumala Nayaka; blends Islamic and Dravidian styles. 82-foot columns; intricate ceiling paintings.

name: Doddabetta Peak
description: The highest peak in the Nilgiris at 2,623 metres elevation, located 10 km from Ooty. Offers panoramic views of the surrounding hills and valleys on clear days.

name: Government Botanical Gardens
description: A 55-acre botanical garden established in 1897 featuring rare tree species, a 20-million-year-old fossilized tree, Italian-style gardens, and orchid displays. Hosts an annual flower show in May.

name: Ooty Lake
description: An artificial lake built in 1824 offering paddle boats, rowboats, and motorboat rides. Popular spot for families and couples seeking leisurely water activities.

name: Bichitrapur Mangrove Reserve
description: Odisha's second largest mangrove forest 10 km from Talasari. Boating through winding waterways to observe birdlife and dense mangrove vegetation in their natural habitat.

name: Subarnarekha River Mouth
description: Where Subarnarekha River flows into the Bay of Bengal. Scenic spot for photography and observing river-sea convergence with fishing activities.

name: Talasari Beach
description: Pristine unspoiled beach where Subarnarekha River meets the Bay of Bengal at the Odisha-Bengal border. Casuarina groves and red crabs; minimal tourist traffic.

name: Beypore Beach and Lighthouse
description: Quiet fishing village beach with traditional boats anchored. Historic lighthouse on the headland. Sunset views. Less touristy than nearby Calicut beach.

name: Beypore Uru Shipyard
description: Traditional dhow (uru) shipbuilding centre active for 1,000+ years. Hand-built 500-tonne wooden vessels using teak and jackwood by master craftsmen (ustads). Boats exported to the Gulf.

name: Dongria Kondh Villages
description: About 100 villages of the Dongria Kondh PVTG community scattered through Niyamgiri Hills. Tourism through licensed guides supports community livelihoods while respecting traditions.

name: Niyamgiri Hills
description: 250 sq km hill range sacred to the Dongria Kondh tribe. Perennial streams and springs originate here; bauxite-capped peaks offer scenic views. Responsible trekking available with community guides.

name: Mahaganapati Temple
description: The largest of the eight Ashtavinayak temples, where sunrays enter the inner sanctum on Surya-Sankranti. The idol has 10 trunks and 20 hands in its hidden form. Engineered to align with the sun at specific times of year.

name: Pataleshwar Caves
description: Ancient rock-cut caves in Pune (near Ranjangaon route), featuring a Shiva temple carved into the mountainside. Dating from around the 8th-9th century, the site shows intricate stone carvings and tunnel networks.

name: Undavalli Caves
description: Four-story rock-cut caves from the 4th-5th century featuring monolithic 20-foot reclining Vishnu statue on serpent Ananta. Important Gupta-era monument with elephant carvings.
